title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: Many applications stop one two extremes: simple historical summaries little economic structure complex risk engines hard explain harder package scenario2risk sits middle. uses factor-augmented VAR framework connect macro conditions asset returns, exposes model small set user-facing functions.

title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: package created around three practical design ideas: Macro conditions matter portfolio risk, model accept flexible set macro predictors instead historical asset returns. Users usually care portfolio loss summaries VaR expected shortfall, raw simulated return paths. compact package still provide model checking, scenario-based VaR output can compared realized rolling losses. leads two core workflows: portfolio_risk() scenario-based terminal-loss measurement model_check() rolling VaR exceedance comparisons

title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: Align macro predictors asset returns date. Extract small number macro factors using principal components. Fit VAR model macro factors asset returns. Simulate future scenario paths. Aggregate simulated asset returns portfolio-level losses. Summarize downside risk compare VaR exceedances. next two sections walk package’s main workflows.

title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: start estimating scenario-based terminal-loss risk 12-month horizon. returned object contains two main pieces: risk_summary: one-row table risk metrics loss_distribution: one simulated terminal loss per scenari Printing returned object gives us risk summary. portfolio_risk() summary contains: mean_loss: average simulated terminal loss median_loss: median simulated terminal loss probability_of_loss: share scenarios positive loss var_95: 95% Value--Risk terminal loss es_95: 95% Expected Shortfall Together, measures summarize center downside tail simulated loss distribution. can also visualize simulated loss distribution:  plot, histogram shows simulated distribution terminal portfolio loss, vertical red line marks estimated 95% VaR.
code: risk <- portfolio_risk(   macro_data = demo_macro_data,   return_data = demo_return_data,   portfolio = demo_portfolio_weights,   horizon = 12,   n_scenarios = 200,   k = 2,   var_lag = 1,   seed = 123 )  risk #> portfolio risk #> -------------- #>  #> Terminal-loss risk metrics: #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   mean_loss median_loss probability_of_loss var_95 es_95 #>       <dbl>       <dbl>               <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> #> 1   -0.0802     -0.0740               0.195 0.0779 0.102 plot_portfolio_risk(risk)

title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: Scenario-based risk estimates useful checked realized outcomes. model_check() function performs rolling historical evaluation: forecast origin, model refit previous window months future portfolio losses simulated chosen horizon resulting scenario-based VaR compared realized forward loss comparison repeated historical simulation benchmark output reports realized exceedance frequency : FAVAR scenario model historical simulation benchmark can visualize comparison:  dashed red line marks expected 5% exceedance rate 95% VaR model.
code: check <- model_check(   macro_data = demo_macro_data,   return_data = demo_return_data,   portfolio = demo_portfolio_weights,   horizon = 6,   n_scenarios = 50,   k = 2,   var_lag = 1,   seed = 123,   window = 120,   n_origins = 6 )  check #> rolling model check #> ------------------- #>  #> VaR exceedance rate: #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   model            var_95_exceedance expected_exceedance n_origins n_exceedances #>   <chr>                        <dbl>               <dbl>     <int>         <int> #> 1 favar_scenario                   0                0.05         6             0 #> 2 historical_simu…                 0                0.05         6             0 plot_model_check(check)

title: A Tour of scenario2risk
text: Several arguments control behavior workflows: horizon: forecast horizon months n_scenarios: number simulated scenario paths k: number macro factors retained var_lag: lag length VAR window: rolling estimation window used model_check() n_origins: number rolling forecast origins used model_check()

title: Macro-Financial Scenario Portfolio Risk Analysis
text: scenario2risk estimates downside portfolio risk simulated macro-financial scenarios. package combines principal component analysis factor-augmented VAR model generate future equity, bond, cash return paths, summarizes terminal-loss risk rolling VaR exceedance diagnostics. designed simple three-asset setting equity, bond, cash weights, focuses two practical tasks: estimating terminal portfolio loss risk simulated macro-financial scenarios checking often scenario-based VaR exceeded relative realized historical outcomes

title: Check VaR exceedance rates — model_check
text: model_check() performs rolling, horizon-aligned VaR exceedance check. historical forecast origin, fits FAVAR model previous window months, simulates h-horizon portfolio losses, compares resulting 95 percent VaR realized h-horizon portfolio loss. also reports exceedance rate Historical Simulation VaR benchmark.

code: model_check(   macro_data,   return_data,   portfolio,   horizon = 12,   n_scenarios = 300,   k = 2,   var_lag = 1,   seed = 123,   window = 120,   n_origins = 36 )

title: Check VaR exceedance rates — model_check
text: macro_data data frame contains date macro predictor columns. return_data data frame date, equity_return, bond_return, cash_return columns. portfolio data frame contains weights required assets equity, bond, cash. horizon Integer VaR horizon months. Default 12. n_scenarios Integer number simulated FAVAR paths rolling forecast origin. Default 300. k Integer number principal-component macro factors used FAVAR state vector. Default 2. var_lag Integer lag order VAR fitted macro factors asset returns. Default 1. seed Integer random seed used bootstrap simulation. Default 123. window Integer rolling estimation window months. Default 120. n_origins Integer number recent forecast origins check. Default 36.
